Fact: Donuts applied through subsidiaries for 307 new gTLD strings; ICANN dispute material identifies Google with 101 applications and Amazon with 78.
Interpretation: Largest applicant by a wide margin. Applications are not the same as TLDs ultimately awarded or operated.

Fact: Donuts stated that economies of scale across many niche strings were central to its strategy.
Interpretation: High fixed registry costs and common distribution channels can reward portfolio scale.

Fact: Donuts acquired Rightside, expanding both TLD assets and registry capabilities.
Interpretation: Acquisitions can concentrate registry agreements and operating capabilities after the application round itself.
The combination joined a large gTLD portfolio with significant registry-service infrastructure.

Fact: Donuts and Afilias rebranded under the Identity Digital name.
Interpretation: One corporate identity now spans portfolio operations and registry-service infrastructure.

Fact: Identity Digital describes its portfolio as nearly 300 TLDs.
Interpretation: Portfolio scale is a measure of breadth across TLD namespaces; it is distinct from technical RSP scale and from registrations under those TLDs.

Fact: ICANN describes Identity Digital as the world’s largest TLD registry operator.
Interpretation: This supports the current operator-scale characterization; it is not a statement about control over ICANN policy or the DNS root.

Fact: Identity Digital says it manages 460+ gTLDs, ccTLDs and dotBrands as a registry services provider.
Interpretation: Backend management can include TLDs that Identity Digital does not own or operate contractually.

Fact: Identity Digital lists its headquarters in Bellevue, Washington.
Interpretation: Corporate headquarters are one geography; DNS serving is distributed.

Fact: Populate the largest 2026 legal applicant from official public ICANN application data.
Interpretation: Compare directly with Donuts’ 307 applications in 2012.

Fact: Normalize applications by public direct / ultimate parent company where the ICANN data supports it.
Interpretation: Keep corporate-group ranking separate from legal-applicant ranking.

Fact: .com and .net together had 179.1 million registered domain names at the end of Q2 2026; .com alone had 166.6 million.
Interpretation: A small number of TLD strings can carry enormous second-level registration volume; portfolio breadth and registration depth are different forms of scale.

Fact: IANA lists Verisign as operator of A-root and J-root; Verisign also acts as the Root Zone Maintainer implementing validated root-zone changes.
Interpretation: Operational concentration at the root layer is distinct from ICANN policy-making and from ownership or operation of TLD portfolios.
